paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think this whole passage is about: God's work keeps going when His people change. Elijah is taken up in a whirlwind, and Elisha is left standing on the riverbank holding a cloak. That's a big moment. But Elisha doesn't wait for a sign from somebody else. He picks up the cloak, strikes the water, and asks, "Where now is the LORD, the God of Elijah?" (2 Kings 2:14).

And look at how he got there. Three times Elijah says, "Please stay here," and three times Elisha says, "I will not leave you" (2 Kings 2:2, 4, 6). He stuck close right up to the end, and he was watching when it counted (2 Kings 2:10-12). I'm not telling you to follow a person everywhere like a lost puppy, baker. I'm saying the ones who show up and pay attention are the ones ready when it's their turn to step up.

Now, the passage ends with some HEAVY moments, and I think this one is hard to read. Still, the line that matters is that the LORD's word through Elisha healed the spring, and "the waters there have been healthy to this day" (2 Kings 2:21-22). So the lesson for you is this: God is the one who keeps going, even when the people around you come and go. Stay close, keep your eyes open, and when your turn comes, trust that the God who was with them is with you too.
